title: Shopee & Lazada Marketplace Management Agency APAC: Buyer Guide
summary: Evaluate Shopee and Lazada marketplace management agencies across APAC with real pricing, a scoring framework, and selection criteria from a managed-services operator.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** A strong Shopee Lazada marketplace management agency in APAC should offer multi-market platform expertise, localized content, fulfillment integration, and transparent reporting under client-owned accounts. Budget US$2,000–$15,000/month per market depending on scope, and use a structured scoring framework across speed, cost, scalability, and knowledge retention.


---


## What Success Actually Looks Like Before You Hire


A well-run Shopee and Lazada operation in Southeast Asia typically achieves 15–25% month-over-month GMV growth in the first six months, maintains advertising cost of sale (ACoS) below 12%, and sustains a store health score above 4.7 out of 5. I know this because we've managed marketplace stores across six APAC markets for brands like Chow Sang Sang and HomePlus, and those are the benchmarks we hold ourselves to.

But here's the uncomfortable truth: most brands searching for a Shopee Lazada marketplace management agency in APAC don't actually know what they're buying. The agency landscape in Southeast Asia ranges from solo freelancers running Seller Center from a co-working space to full-stack operations teams with warehouse integration and real-time analytics dashboards. The price spread is equally dramatic — from US$500/month to US$15,000/month — and the correlation between cost and quality is weaker than you'd expect.


This guide exists to give you a structured framework to evaluate your options. Whether you're a US or European brand entering Southeast Asia, or an APAC-based company scaling across Shopee and Lazada's regional footprint, you'll walk away with concrete evaluation criteria, real pricing benchmarks, and a scoring system you can use in your next vendor review.


The APAC B2C e-commerce market is projected to reach US$4.86 trillion by 2026 according to Anchanto's marketplace analysis. That figure is large enough to attract every variety of agency — the excellent and the mediocre alike. Your job is to tell them apart.


## Five Evaluation Criteria That Actually Matter


Before comparing agencies, you need a shared vocabulary for what "good" means. After working across marketplace engagements in Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Malaysia, I've distilled this down to five dimensions.


### 1. Market Coverage and Platform Depth


Shopee and Lazada operate differently in every country. Shopee Philippines has distinct campaign mechanics from Shopee Thailand. Lazada's LazMall onboarding process in Vietnam differs from Malaysia. A credible agency should demonstrate operational experience — not just theoretical knowledge — in your target markets.


Ask for evidence: store dashboards, campaign reports, or platform partner certifications. Lazada's preferred partner program, for instance, grants agencies like GroupM preferential access and early feature rollouts according to Lazada's official partnership announcements. Shopee's Partner Programme similarly tiers agencies by verified GMV managed.


### 2. Operational Scope: Listings, Ads, Fulfillment, or All Three


Some agencies handle only content and advertising. Others extend into inventory syncing, fulfillment coordination, and customer service. The distinction matters because marketplace management in SEA isn't just a marketing function — it's an operations function.


When we onboarded a Hong Kong-based FMCG brand onto Shopee and Lazada across four markets in 2023, the real bottleneck wasn't ad spend optimization — it was synchronizing inventory across Shopee Fulfillment by Shopee (FBS), Lazada's own fulfillment centers, and the brand's 3PL partner in each country. That integration work took our team eight weeks using a combination of Anchanto's OMS and custom API connectors to Seller Center.

If your agency can't speak to API-level integration or at least tool-level automation (Ginee, Anchanto, Sellercraft), they're likely managing stores manually — which doesn't scale past two or three markets.

### 3. Advertising Competence Across Shopee Ads and Lazada Sponsored Solutions


Shopee Ads (keyword ads, discovery ads, shop ads) and Lazada Sponsored Solutions operate on fundamentally different auction models. Shopee's CPC bidding has shifted significantly since their 2023 algorithm updates, while Lazada's Sponsored Discovery uses a cost-per-impression model that rewards high-CTR creatives.


A strong Shopee Lazada agency should be able to show you:


- ACoS benchmarks by category and market
- Campaign structure methodology (how they segment branded vs. generic keywords)
- Incrementality measurement (what sales would have happened without ad spend)


According to the Asia-Pacific B2C Ecommerce Market Report 2025–2029 published via Yahoo Finance, paid marketplace advertising spend in SEA grew 34% year-over-year in 2024. That growth means more competition per keyword and higher stakes for getting campaign structure right.


### 4. Content Localization Quality


This is where most agencies from outside the region fail. A product listing that converts in Singapore (English-dominant, price-sensitive, review-driven) won't work in Thailand (Thai-language, visual-heavy, flash-sale-driven) or Vietnam (Vietnamese-language, voucher-stacking culture, livestream-influenced).


Evaluate localization capability by reviewing actual live listings the agency has produced — not portfolio PDFs, but real Shopee and Lazada product pages you can inspect for keyword density, image quality, A+ content usage, and review response handling.


### 5. Reporting Transparency and Data Ownership


Do you own the Seller Center accounts, or does the agency? This isn't a minor contractual detail — it's a strategic question. If the agency owns the accounts, your store reviews, seller ratings, and advertising history stay with them when you part ways.


Insist on owning all platform accounts. A reputable marketplace management agency in APAC will operate under your accounts with sub-user access, not the other way around.

## Pricing Benchmarks: What Agencies Actually Charge in 2025


Pricing transparency in this market is poor, so I'll share what we see across competitive bids and our own engagements. These figures represent Southeast Asian market rates as of Q1 2025.


### Retainer-Only Models


- **Freelancer / Solo Operator** : US$500–$1,500/month per market. Typically handles listing uploads and basic ad management. No fulfillment integration. Common in the Philippines and Vietnam.
- **Boutique Agency (5–20 staff)** : US$2,000–$5,000/month per market. Covers content, ads, and basic reporting. May support 2–3 platforms. Strong in single-market depth.
- **Regional Agency (20–100 staff)** : US$4,000–$10,000/month per market. Full-stack operations including fulfillment coordination, customer service, and cross-market campaign planning.
- **Enterprise Managed Services** : US$8,000–$15,000+/month per market. Dedicated team model with named account managers, custom analytics dashboards, and SLA-backed response times.


### Commission-Based Models


Many agencies in SEA charge a base retainer plus 3–8% of GMV as a performance commission. This aligns incentives but can become expensive at scale. A brand doing US$200,000/month GMV on Shopee Thailand at a 5% commission rate is paying US$10,000/month in variable fees alone — on top of retainer.


### Hidden Costs to Budget For


- **Platform commission** : Shopee charges 2–6% depending on category and market; Lazada charges 1–4% plus payment fees according to their respective seller fee schedules
- **Advertising spend** : Separate from agency fees. Budget 8–15% of target GMV for ads in the first 6 months
- **Content production** : Photography, video, translation — often quoted separately at US$500–$2,000/month per market
- **Fulfillment fees** : FBS/LGS fees vary by market; budget US$1.50–$4.00 per order


## The Decision Matrix: In-House vs. Agency vs. Managed Team


The real decision most brands face isn't which agency to hire — it's whether to hire one at all. Here's a scoring framework we use with clients weighing their options.


### Scoring Framework (Rate Each 1–5)


**Speed to Market**


- In-House Team: 2/5 — Recruiting in-market takes 3–6 months per country
- Marketplace Agency: 4/5 — Onboarding in 2–4 weeks typical
- Managed Contracting Team: 5/5 — Pre-built team, deploys in 1–2 weeks


**Cost Efficiency (Year 1)**


- In-House Team: 2/5 — Salary, benefits, office, tools add up to US$8,000–$15,000/month per market before ad spend
- Marketplace Agency: 4/5 — Retainer model keeps fixed costs predictable
- Managed Contracting Team: 3/5 — Higher retainer than pure agency, lower than full in-house


**Institutional Knowledge Retention**


- In-House Team: 5/5 — Knowledge stays with the company
- Marketplace Agency: 2/5 — Knowledge walks out when the contract ends
- Managed Contracting Team: 4/5 — Team is dedicated to you; knowledge transfer is contractual


**Scalability Across Markets**


- In-House Team: 2/5 — Each new market requires local hiring and entity setup
- Marketplace Agency: 4/5 — Regional agencies cover multiple markets from one contract
- Managed Contracting Team: 5/5 — Scale headcount up or down without entity obligations


**Platform Expertise Depth**


- In-House Team: 3/5 — Depends entirely on who you hire
- Marketplace Agency: 4/5 — Daily exposure across multiple brands and categories
- Managed Contracting Team: 4/5 — Dedicated specialists with cross-client pattern recognition


**Total Score**


- In-House: 14/25
- Agency: 18/25
- Managed Team: 21/25


The managed contracting model scores highest on paper, but it's not right for every brand. If your GMV per market is below US$50,000/month, a boutique agency or even a capable freelancer may deliver better ROI. The managed team model shines when you're operating in three or more markets simultaneously and need consistent execution quality.

## A Branch8 Implementation: What the First 90 Days Look Like


To make this concrete, here's what happened when a Japanese beauty brand engaged us to launch on Shopee and Lazada across Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines in Q3 2024.


**Weeks 1–2** : Account audit and market prioritization. We discovered their existing Lazada Malaysia store had a 3.2 seller rating due to unmanaged customer inquiries — a 90-day recovery plan was required before any ad spend made sense.


**Weeks 3–4** : Listing migration using Ginee (multi-platform listing tool) to push 340 SKUs across all four Shopee markets simultaneously. Content was localized in-house by our teams in each market, not machine-translated.


**Weeks 5–8** : Campaign launch timed to Shopee 9.9 and Lazada's mid-month sale. We structured campaigns using a three-tier keyword architecture: branded terms (lowest ACoS, ~4%), category terms (moderate, ~10%), and competitor conquesting terms (highest risk, ~18% ACoS but strong for awareness).


**Weeks 9–12** : Fulfillment optimization. We migrated from merchant-fulfilled to FBS in Singapore and Philippines, reducing average delivery time from 5.2 days to 2.1 days. Conversion rate increased 22% in those two markets — faster delivery is the single most underrated conversion lever on Shopee.


By the end of 90 days, combined GMV across four markets reached US$127,000/month, up from US$18,000/month at the start. The brand's total monthly cost for our managed team was US$24,000 across all four markets — roughly 19% of GMV, which they expected to drop below 12% by month nine as organic rankings matured.


## Red Flags When Evaluating a Shopee Lazada Marketplace Management Agency


### They Can't Show Live Store Examples


Portfolio decks with blurred-out brand names and screenshots from 2022 aren't evidence. Ask to see live Shopee or Lazada stores they're actively managing. Check the store's rating, response rate, and listing quality yourself.


### They Promise Specific GMV Guarantees


No legitimate agency can guarantee GMV because marketplace algorithms, competitor behavior, and platform promotions are outside anyone's control. Agencies that guarantee specific revenue numbers are either lying or planning to buy their way there with unsustainable ad spend.


### They Don't Distinguish Between Markets


If an agency pitches the same strategy for Shopee Philippines and Shopee Thailand, walk away. According to e-Conomy SEA 2024 by Google, Temasek, and Bain, the Philippines' e-commerce GMV grew 20% year-over-year while Thailand grew 13% — different growth rates require different approaches to inventory depth, pricing, and campaign intensity.


### They Resist Giving You Account Ownership


I mentioned this earlier, but it's worth repeating because it's the most common structural mistake brands make when engaging their first Shopee Lazada agency in APAC. If the agency insists on owning the Seller Center accounts, your negotiating position degrades every month as your store equity accumulates in their hands.


### They Have No Technical Integration Capability


Managing stores through the Seller Center web UI doesn't scale. At minimum, an agency should use a multi-channel listing tool (Ginee, Anchanto, Linnworks) and ideally have API integration capability for order management and inventory sync. Manual copy-paste operations lead to overselling, listing errors, and fulfillment delays.

## How Market-Specific Dynamics Shape Your Agency Choice


### Philippines: Volume Play, Tight Margins


Shopee dominates the Philippines with over 73% of marketplace traffic according to iPrice Group's Map of E-commerce data. Lazada runs second but maintains a stronger LazMall presence for premium brands. Agencies specializing in the Philippines market need deep fluency in Tagalog/Filipino content and an understanding of the cash-on-delivery (COD) preference that still accounts for over 40% of orders.


### Singapore and Malaysia: Mature, Competitive, Ad-Heavy


These are the most competitive Shopee and Lazada markets. Customer acquisition costs are higher, and organic ranking is harder to achieve without sustained advertising investment. An agency managing Singapore or Malaysia stores should demonstrate ACoS management discipline and experience with cross-border fulfillment from regional warehouses.


### Thailand and Vietnam: High Growth, Localization-Critical


Both markets are growing rapidly but require genuine local-language capability. We've seen brands lose months of momentum in Thailand by launching with Google-Translated listings — Shopee's search algorithm penalizes low-engagement listings, and poorly translated content kills click-through rates before ads even have a chance.


## How to Evaluate Your Next Marketplace Partner


Use the scoring framework above, but overlay it with three final questions:


**First, what's your GMV threshold?** If you're below US$30,000/month per market, a boutique agency at US$2,000–$3,000/month gives you the best cost-to-capability ratio. Above US$100,000/month, a managed team model with dedicated headcount starts making financial sense because the commission component of agency fees becomes punitive.


**Second, how many markets are you operating in simultaneously?** Single-market operations can be handled by local specialists. Three or more markets require either a regional agency or a managed contracting partner who can coordinate campaigns, inventory, and promotions across countries without you becoming the project manager.


**Third, what's your exit plan?** Every marketplace engagement should have a defined transition path — either to in-house, to a different partner, or to a scaled-up version of the current arrangement. If your agency can't articulate what the handover looks like, they haven't thought about your long-term interests.


This guide is for brands doing at least US$10,000/month in marketplace GMV or planning to invest seriously in Southeast Asian e-commerce. If you're testing the waters with a handful of SKUs and no committed ad budget, an agency engagement is premature — start with Seller Center directly, learn the mechanics, and then bring in professional help when you've validated demand.
